meta.title: Conductive collagen/polypyrrole-b-polycaprolactone hydrogel for bioprinting of neural tissue constructs.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: A conductive bioink of collagen with polypyrrole-block-polycaprolactone was developed for printing neural tissue constructs; adding the conductive polymer raised the gel's modulus and print fidelity.

formulations.stiffness_note: modulus rises with PPy-b-PCL; highest at 2%
formulations.review_notes: Cell type and viability not found in the extracted text; check the paper.
formulations.name: 4% collagen + PPy-b-PCL (conductive)
formulations.key_outcome: Conductive polymer increased the collagen ink's mechanical integrity for neural constructs.

evidence.quote: A concentration of 4% (w/v) Collagen Type 1 was used.
the mechanical integrity of the collagen hydrogel increases with increasing concentration of PPy-b-PCL
